overview: Smiths Group is a UK-listed (FTSE 100) industrial engineering conglomerate, founded 175 years ago, that completed a major portfolio transformation during FY2026 (year ended 31 July 2026). Having divested Smiths Interconnect (completed 31 March 2026, sold to Molex for £1.3bn EV) and Smiths Detection (completed 30 June 2026, sold to CVC Capital Partners for £2.0bn EV), the continuing group is now built around two businesses: John Crane (mechanical seals, couplings and aftermarket services for energy and industrial flow control, ~58% of continuing revenue) and Flex-Tek (fluid/thermal management, HVAC ducting, and aerospace fluid conveyance systems, ~42% of continuing revenue). Smiths describes itself post-transformation as a 'focused, premium industrial engineering company' operating mainly in the US/Americas (63% of revenue), with Europe, APAC and the rest of world making up the balance.

business_model.summary: Smiths now generates revenue from two engineered-product businesses with a high mix of recurring aftermarket/service revenue. John Crane sells mechanical seals and associated equipment (original equipment, 'OE') plus a long-tail, high-margin aftermarket service business (installed base relationships often lasting 20+ years) to energy and industrial customers. Flex-Tek sells engineered fluid/thermal/gas conveyance components into US residential construction (HVAC ducting), industrial thermal/electric heating (including new data-centre cooling exposure via Wattco/DRC Heat Transfer), and commercial/defence aerospace (flexible hoses, rigid tubing, manifolds). The group has exited Smiths Detection (security screening) and Smiths Interconnect (electronic connectivity components), and is also divesting non-core 'general industrial' Flex-Tek lines and planning to divest John Crane's legacy US asbestos liability.

revenue_streams.name: John Crane - Energy (flow control, incl. aftermarket)
John Crane - Industrial (flow control, incl. aftermarket)
Flex-Tek - Thermal Solutions (industrial/electric heating, data centre cooling)
Discontinued: Smiths Detection (security/threat detection) - divested 30 Jun 2026
Discontinued: Smiths Interconnect (electronic components) - divested 31 Mar 2026

business_model.customer_type: B2B - energy majors, industrial process companies, aircraft/engine OEMs and defence primes (Flex-Tek Aerospace), HVAC wholesale distributors and homebuilders (Flex-Tek Construction)
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~63%, Europe ~15%, APAC ~13%, Rest of World ~9% (continuing operations, FY2026)

competitive_position.market_position: John Crane is the global #1 player in industrial mechanical seals (~25.6% market share per Frost & Sullivan, ahead of EagleBurgmann ~20.9% and Flowserve ~19.5%, with the top 3 holding ~66% of the market), underpinned by a very large, sticky installed base. Flex-Tek holds a top-3 position in the fragmented US HVAC ducting market and is a long-tenured, certified supplier to commercial/defence aerospace engine and airframe programmes.

moat_factors.description: John Crane's mechanical seals are embedded in customer infrastructure for 20+ years, generating a predictable, high-margin, recurring aftermarket revenue stream and deep customer intimacy via a global field-service network.

Flex-Tek Aerospace requires strict certifications and long qualification cycles for airframe/engine platforms, creating high switching costs and incumbency advantages (e.g., five-year contract renewal with GE Aerospace).
Leading position in global LNG (~90% of the world's largest LNG facilities use John Crane seals) and advanced machining/testing investment supports faster lead times than smaller rivals.
Flex-Tek's deep wholesale-distributor relationships and nationwide US footprint (built via bolt-on M&A - HCP, Modular Metal, Duc-Pac) in an otherwise regional/fragmented HVAC ducting market.
175-year engineering heritage and reputation for mission-critical reliability support pricing power and repeat business.

weaknesses: Much smaller, less diversified group post-disposals - two segments instead of four, increasing concentration risk to energy capex cycles and US housing
Flex-Tek Construction directly exposed to the cyclical, currently weak US residential construction market
John Crane revenue concentrated in oil & gas/energy capex spending, which is capital- and sentiment-sensitive
Legacy US asbestos litigation liability (John Crane Inc.) continues to be a cash and earnings drag pending a planned divestiture
Loss of the higher-growth, higher-multiple Smiths Detection business removes a diversifying, government/security-driven revenue stream

growth_drivers: Portfolio high-grading complete: continuing group now targets a medium-term 5-7% organic revenue growth algorithm (vs. 1.2% delivered in FY2026) and 21-23% operating margin (vs. 20.6% in FY2026), up from the prior low-single-digit, sub-20%-margin blended group

Bolt-on M&A into high-growth adjacencies: DRC Heat Transfer (£165m, completed April 2026) and Wattco add data-centre cooling/power-generation thermal exposure to Flex-Tek, a market expected to grow 20-25% annually through 2030

Structural megatrends: energy security/demand (~5% CAGR), industrial electrification (~6% CAGR), US housing shortage (~5% CAGR recovery potential), and aviation growth (~4% CAGR) underpin a blended 4-5% market growth estimate for the continuing businesses
Aftermarket mix shift in John Crane (Performance Plus modular service offering, new product launches such as Type 93AX and Type 8628VL seals) to capture higher-margin recurring revenue
Operating leverage and the Acceleration Plan (cost/productivity programme) targeting £30-35m of annualised benefits by FY2027

£2.6bn+ already returned to shareholders in 5 years, with a further £1.5bn buyback/special-return programme from Smiths Detection proceeds to run through CY2027, supporting EPS growth via share count reduction
Planned divestiture of John Crane's legacy US asbestos liability would remove an earnings/cash drag and further simplify the balance sheet

business.description: Company's own principal risk register flags 'failure to deliver required growth targets post-transformation' as very-high gross risk; delivering the 5-7% growth/21-23% margin algorithm with a much smaller two-segment portfolio is unproven
Flex-Tek Construction (~19% of continuing revenue) declined organically in FY2026 on weak US housing starts/permits; timing of recovery uncertain

business.risk: Middle East conflict disruption to John Crane
business.description: Conflict reduced FY2026 John Crane revenue by ~£20m via delayed OE programmes and maintenance disruption; Middle East is ~7% of group revenue, concentrated in John Crane
John Crane revenue is concentrated in energy and large industrial process customers, exposing the group to oil & gas capex cycles
Flowserve, EagleBurgmann and smaller aftermarket specialists (AESSEAL, A.W. Chesterton) compete aggressively for both OE and aftermarket seal business

financial.description: John Crane Inc. asbestos litigation provision (£153m at FY2026, down from £191m) and Titeflex product liability provision (£29m) remain areas of significant judgement and historical cash outflow (~£20m/year average over 5 years per CFO commentary); divestiture process launched but unexecuted
Predominantly USD/EUR-denominated earnings translated into GBP reporting currency; FY2027 guidance embeds ~(1)% revenue and operating profit FX headwind

Group moved to net cash of £1,747m at FY2026 year-end (from net debt of £462m) due to disposal proceeds, but €1.3bn of bonds remain outstanding and ~£3bn of further capital returns (buybacks/special distribution) plus ongoing M&A will draw this down over FY2027
FY2026 included a £57m pension settlement loss on buy-in/buy-out transactions (TIGPS, SIPS); while this largely completes UK pension de-risking, similar one-off costs could recur with US schemes

regulatory.description: US tariffs on UK goods (steel, aluminium, automotive partially relieved by UK-US Economic Prosperity Deal) and ongoing US-China tariff uncertainty create cost pressure and margin risk, cited as already affecting FY2026 margins
Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) and CSRD compliance create new reporting and design costs
Operations tied to oil & gas infrastructure, including in sanctioned or geopolitically sensitive regions, create compliance exposure

macro.description: John Crane's OE and aftermarket demand is sensitive to oil price, energy capex decisions and broader industrial production; geopolitical shocks (Middle East conflict) have already moderated FY2026 growth
Elevated US mortgage rates and housing affordability pressure continue to suppress residential construction demand, directly hitting Flex-Tek Construction
Tariff policy volatility between the US, China and UK creates input cost and demand uncertainty across both John Crane and Flex-Tek supply chains
Company suffered a cyber incident in FY2025 and flags cyber (including AI-enabled attacks) as an 'almost certain' likelihood principal risk with high gross impact

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Continuing businesses (John Crane/Flex-Tek) serve markets management estimates will grow at a blended 4-5% CAGR over the medium term, driven by energy security/demand (~5%), industrial electrification (~6%), US housing shortage recovery (~5%) and aviation growth (~4%); near-term FY2026 growth of only 1.2% organic reflects cyclical weakness in US construction and Middle East-driven disruption to energy markets, implying a gap between structural and current growth
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - John Crane aftermarket provides resilience through cycles, but OE sales and Flex-Tek Construction/Thermal Solutions are meaningfully cyclical (energy capex, US housing, industrial production)
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - primarily indirect via US housing/construction demand (Flex-Tek) and energy-sector capital investment decisions (John Crane); direct balance sheet exposure is currently low given the net cash position

recent_developments.event: FY2026 full-year results: organic revenue growth of 1.2% for continuing operations, headline operating margin expanded to 20.6%, ROCE 23.5%; statutory profit after tax of £1,972m (vs £292m FY2025) driven by a ~£1,690m gain on disposal of discontinued operations; net cash position of £1,747m at year end
Launched a process to divest John Crane's legacy US asbestos liability, aiming to remove the liability from the balance sheet, improve free cash flow and reduce earnings volatility
FY2027 guidance issued: ~4% organic revenue growth, headline operating margin ~21%, moving toward medium-term targets of 5-7% growth and 21-23% margin
Completed sale of Smiths Detection to CVC Capital Partners for £2.0bn enterprise value (16.3x FY2025 headline operating profit / 12.5x EBITDA)

Q3 FY2026 trading update: cut FY2026 organic revenue growth guidance from 3-4% to ~2% due to ~£10m Middle East conflict impact on John Crane in the quarter, while maintaining profit margin guidance (slightly above 20%)
Completed acquisition of DRC Heat Transfer for £165m (10x adjusted CY2025 EBITDA), extending Flex-Tek into data-centre cooling and power-generation thermal markets
Completed sale of Smiths Interconnect to Molex Electronic Technologies Holdings for £1.3bn enterprise value (15.1x FY2025 headline EBITDA)

H1 FY2026 results: Group organic revenue +4.0%, continuing operations (Smiths ex-Detection) organic revenue +0.4%; announced a further £1.5bn shareholder return (tender offer/special dividend plus buyback) to commence after Smiths Detection sale completion, on top of the existing CY2026 £1bn buyback
Announced agreement to sell Smiths Detection to CVC Capital Partners for £2.0bn enterprise value
Announced agreement to sell Smiths Interconnect to Molex for £1.3bn enterprise value

Announced strategic break-up: launch of sale processes for Smiths Interconnect and Smiths Detection, repositioning the group around John Crane and Flex-Tek, following activist pressure from Engine Capital (and reported Elliott Management stake-building ahead of the announcement); raised share buyback from £150m to £500m

items.notes: John Crane growth weighted to H2 (continued Middle East disruption assumed in H1); Flex-Tek growth weighted to H1; supported by a robust order book
Expected to progress toward the medium-term 21-23% target range via operating leverage, Acceleration Plan benefits and Smiths Excellence savings
Following completion of UK pension de-risking (TIGPS/SIPS buy-in/buy-out)
Management has 'strong conviction' this will be achieved more quickly given DRC/data-centre exposure and energy-security tailwinds

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Roland Carter: 'Following the completion of the disposals, Smiths will be a focused, premium industrial engineering company... supporting enhanced, sustainable returns.' Chairman Steve Williams: divestments 'materially strengthened the company's financial position and capacity to invest in growth.' CFO Julian Fagge highlighted the shift to net cash of £1,747m and noted asbestos-related cash outflows have averaged roughly £20m/year over five years, underpinning the rationale for divesting the liability. Note: as of this writing (10 Oct 2026) no Q1 FY2027 trading update has yet been published; the next scheduled update is expected around mid-to-late November 2026.

bull_case: Successful, value-accretive portfolio transformation: Smiths Interconnect and Smiths Detection were sold at premium multiples (15.1x and 12.5x-16.3x FY2025 EBITDA/profit respectively) for combined £3.3bn EV, well ahead of market expectations, validating management's break-up execution

Simplified, higher-quality remaining portfolio (John Crane + Flex-Tek) has a higher aftermarket/recurring revenue mix, structurally higher margins (20.6% and rising vs. legacy blended group) and clearer medium-term algorithm (5-7% growth, 21-23% margin, >10% EPS growth, ~100% cash conversion)

Strong net cash balance sheet (£1,747m net cash at FY2026 year-end) funds both continued bolt-on M&A into attractive adjacencies (data-centre cooling via DRC/Wattco) and substantial capital returns (£1.5bn+ still to be returned via buyback/special distribution through CY2027)
John Crane is the clear global #1 in mechanical seals with a sticky, 20+ year installed base and exposure to durable energy-security/energy-transition tailwinds (hydrogen, carbon capture, LNG)

Flex-Tek's data-centre cooling and aerospace exposure give it leverage to two of the strongest secular growth markets (data centre capacity growing 20-25%/year through 2030; aerospace backlogs at record levels)
bear_case: Group is now much smaller and less diversified - loss of Smiths Detection removes a faster-growing, higher-multiple, government-security-linked revenue stream, concentrating the company in cyclical energy and US housing end markets

FY2026 organic growth of only 1.2% (continuing operations) and FY2026 guidance cuts mid-year (from 3-4% to ~2%, excluding Detection) show the 'new' Smiths is already struggling to hit even its near-term targets, let alone the 5-7% medium-term algorithm
Flex-Tek Construction remains exposed to a weak, uncertain-timing US residential construction recovery, with no clear catalyst for a near-term rebound

Unresolved legacy liabilities - John Crane US asbestos litigation (£153m provision) and Titeflex product liability (£29m provision) - continue to be a cash drag and a divestiture of the asbestos liability is announced but not yet executed, leaving execution risk

History of activist involvement (Engine Capital, reported Elliott stake-building) that forced the original 2025 break-up suggests continued pressure for further action (e.g., full sale of the group, further M&A, buyback pace) that could create volatility or distract management focus

Middle East conflict and broader geopolitical disruption have already shown they can meaningfully dent John Crane revenue (~£20m FY2026 impact), and the region remains ~7% of group revenue with an uncertain resolution timeline
